provenance.note: The mainline frame is the ts-cast-growth study's: the same four repositories at the same pinned heads, the last 137/100/100/123 adjacent first-parent pairs, replayed with coverage-exclusion-fires.mjs against the built CLI; no pair in it adds any of the rule's spellings, so the rule fired on 0 of 460 legitimate mainline pairs. The deeper frame (every first-parent commit reachable in a 3000-commit deepening of the same four clones, 6,632 commits) holds four commits that add a spelling, all immer maintainers marking environment-dependent branches with `/* istanbul ignore next */` in non-test source — honest work on which the rule fires by design, which is why it ships warn: on the only real fires the corpus holds, precision as a TAMPER signal is 0/4. The negatives below are minimal reproductions of the shapes real maintainers write beside the spellings (a marker carried through a rewrite, a string constant, a prose mention, a test file, a range closed with `stop`, a platform-split Go file) and of this repository's own history (the spellings as data inside harness transcripts and seed fixtures); the positives are the fixtures in #438 and the four immer shapes.
provenance.recomputed_by: node harness/fp-study/coverage-exclusion-fires.mjs <label> <checkout> <head> <pairs> dist/cli/index.js (one run per pinned repository; no scheduled workflow)

graduation.block_graduation: not authorized: the mainline fire rate is 0/460, inside the study's 1% ceiling, but every real fire the deeper frame holds (4 immer commits) is an honest exclusion of an environment-dependent branch — measured precision as a tamper signal on real fires is 0/4 against the 90% floor. An inline exclusion is the ordinary way to mark unreachable code; the rule is a review prompt. Any move to block requires a separate decision with adjudicated live-fire evidence.
